samples.summary: Comment/thread delete routes enforce no author check, contradicting the documented "delete by author only" lifecycle
samples.evidence: `deleteThread` and `deleteComment` take only `@Param`s — no `@Req() req: AuthenticatedRequest` and no comparison of `req.user.id` against `comment.author.userId` — so any workspace member holding a `write`-scoped key can delete another user's thread or reply. `docs/design/sheets/comments.md:32` states the model as "Comment lifecycle: edit / delete by author only", and the editor enforces exactly that (`packages/frontend/src/components/comments/components/CommentThreadCard.tsx:92`: `c.author.userId === currentUserId`). The new surface therefore permits a destructive action the documented design forbids, and it is irreversible (the thread is removed from the CRDT). Every other comment verb in this controller does resolve the caller (`this.author(req)`), which makes the omission look unintentional rather than a decision recorded anywhere in the diff or in notifications.md.

samples.summary: Notification planning + mention parsing reimplemented in the backend instead of shared, so two copies of the same rule now exist
samples.evidence: `planCommentNotifications`, `toUserId` and `MENTION_RE` in comments.controller.ts are line-for-line restatements of `packages/frontend/src/components/comments/notify.ts:29-114` and `mentions.ts`' `MENTION_RE`/`extractMentionedUserIds`. The docblock openly says it "applies the same rule the frontend's notify.ts does", and notifications.md (as amended here) promises "membership authorization, the recipient cap and the dedupe keys stay one implementation" — but the *planning* rule (who is a recipient, mention-vs-reply dedupe, actor exclusion) is now two implementations that must be edited in lockstep. The repo's stated posture is reuse via a shared package (`@wafflebase/core`, and the comment engine itself already lives in `@wafflebase/sheets`, from which this controller imports `createThread`/`addReply`/`deleteComment`), so the planning rule and mention regex had an available shared home. Divergence gives two different answers to "who gets notified for this comment" depending on whether the writer was a browser or an agent.

samples.summary: API-written notifications store the raw mention markup as the preview, unlike the browser path
samples.evidence: `planCommentNotifications` sets `preview: comment.body` verbatim. The frontend equivalent runs `preview()` = `mentionBodyToPlainText(body).slice(0, 200)` (`notify.ts:35-37`, cap comment: "Matches the backend cap"). So a notification produced by an agent comment shows `@[ada](7)` in the inbox where a browser-authored one shows `@ada`, and it relies on `sanitizePreview` for length instead of the shared 200-char rule. Same rule, two visibly different outputs — a divergence from the documented shape, with a small user-visible cost.

samples.summary: Board root shape and seed re-declared in the backend rather than reused from the shared board model
samples.evidence: `BoardMeta`/`BoardDocument`/`initialBoardRoot()` duplicate `YorkieBoardRoot` and `initialBoardRoot()` in `packages/frontend/src/types/board-document.ts:3-10` (same fields, same `'Untitled board'` seed) and overlap `BoardModel` in `packages/board/src/model/board.ts:22-29`, which is exported from `@wafflebase/board`. The docblock admits it "mirrors" the frontend type. Two hand-kept copies of the persisted root shape means a future `meta` field (or a changed default title) has to be added twice or the API silently drops it — `readBoardRoot` already whitelists `title`/`unit`/`recentColors` only. Promotion into `@wafflebase/board` (already a workspace package, with `slides` and `docs` precedent as backend deps) was the available reuse path.

samples.summary: No comment-edit route, although the documented comment lifecycle is edit *and* delete
samples.evidence: `docs/design/sheets/comments.md:32` documents "Comment lifecycle: edit / delete by author only" and the editor exposes both (`CommentThreadCard.tsx:89 canEditOrDelete`, `Comment.editedAt` exists in the model and is copied by `comment-ops.ts#copyComment`). The API offers create/reply/resolve/delete but no `PATCH .../comments/:commentId`, so an agent that mis-writes a comment can only delete and re-post, losing thread position. The class-B audit counted 6 comment items without naming them, so this may be a deliberate scoping choice — but nothing in the diff or a design doc records it.

mergedFrom.summary: No comment-edit route, although the documented comment lifecycle is edit *and* delete
mergedFrom.evidence: `docs/design/sheets/comments.md:32` documents "Comment lifecycle: edit / delete by author only" and the editor exposes both (`CommentThreadCard.tsx:89 canEditOrDelete`, `Comment.editedAt` exists in the model and is copied by `comment-ops.ts#copyComment`). The API offers create/reply/resolve/delete but no `PATCH .../comments/:commentId`, so an agent that mis-writes a comment can only delete and re-post, losing thread position. The class-B audit counted 6 comment items without naming them, so this may be a deliberate scoping choice — but nothing in the diff or a design doc records it.

verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as described. `deleteThread` (comments.controller.ts:388-401) and `deleteComment` (:403-431) accept only `@Param`s — they never inject `@Req() req: AuthenticatedRequest` and never call the controller's own `author(req)` helper (:134-160) or compare against `comment.author.userId`, while every other write verb in the file does (`createThread:247`, `reply:333`, `setResolved:364`). No guard makes this unreachable: `ApiKeyWriteScopeGuard` (api-key-write-scope.guard.ts:38-49) only checks the `write` scope and returns true outright for JWT callers, and `WorkspaceScopeGuard` only binds the key to the route's workspace, so any workspace member with write access can delete another user's thread/reply. The canonical subsystem doc states the opposite model at docs/design/sheets/comments.md:32 ("Comment lifecycle: edit / delete by author only"), and the shipped editor enforces it at CommentThreadCard.tsx:89-93. The write is irreversible through this surface (deleteComment cascades to thread removal at :417-428, applied directly to the CRDT via mutateMap :439-472) and no decision to relax the author rule is recorded in the controller's design commentary (:56-93) or in the design doc. This is in the design-fit lane as an undeclared divergence from the documented lifecycle/data model, and its cost is user-visible data loss rather than internal tidiness, so it is blocking at major.

finding.summary: Notification planning + mention parsing reimplemented in the backend instead of shared, so two copies of the same rule now exist
finding.evidence: `planCommentNotifications`, `toUserId` and `MENTION_RE` in comments.controller.ts are line-for-line restatements of `packages/frontend/src/components/comments/notify.ts:29-114` and `mentions.ts`' `MENTION_RE`/`extractMentionedUserIds`. The docblock openly says it "applies the same rule the frontend's notify.ts does", and notifications.md (as amended here) promises "membership authorization, the recipient cap and the dedupe keys stay one implementation" — but the *planning* rule (who is a recipient, mention-vs-reply dedupe, actor exclusion) is now two implementations that must be edited in lockstep. The repo's stated posture is reuse via a shared package (`@wafflebase/core`, and the comment engine itself already lives in `@wafflebase/sheets`, from which this controller imports `createThread`/`addReply`/`deleteComment`), so the planning rule and mention regex had an available shared home. Divergence gives two different answers to "who gets notified for this comment" depending on whether the writer was a browser or an agent.

verdict.reason: The duplication is real and present as described. comments.controller.ts:504 (MENTION_RE), :511-515 (toUserId, identical to notify.ts:29-33 including docblock), :532-603 (planCommentNotifications, restating notify.ts:50-114 branch-for-branch: resolve->participants minus actor; mention extraction with actor exclusion and dedupe; reply->earlier participants minus actor minus mentioned), and :596-603 participantIds mirroring notify.ts:139-146 uniqueUserIds. The controller's own docblock (comments.controller.ts:520-522) and docs/design/notifications.md:26-29 both state the rule is a restatement of the frontend's, and the doc's claim of "one implementation" covers only membership auth/cap/dedupe keys, not the planning rule. A shared home was available: packages/core/package.json:6 declares the shared foundation package and the backend already consumes @wafflebase/sheets (comments.controller.ts:41-46, packages/backend/package.json:43), so cross-tier reuse is an existing pattern. No guard makes it unreachable; the notify path is invoked on every create/reply/resolve (:290, :320, :351, :383). Duplication/reuse is explicitly in this lens's lane, and the cost lands outside codebase tidiness (divergent recipient sets between browser- and agent-authored comments), so major stands.

finding.summary: comment-ops.ts reimplements thread logic that `@wafflebase/sheets` already owns and exports
finding.evidence: `packages/sheets/src/comment/thread.ts` is the canonical pure thread module — `createThread`, `addReply`, `editComment`, `deleteComment` (root comment ⇒ delete thread, lines 61-76), `setThreadResolved` — and `createThread`/`addReply` are already re-exported from `packages/sheets/src/index.ts:373-374`, which the backend depends on and already imports from (`comments.controller.ts` imports `parseRef`, `cellAnchorToSref`, `Thread`, `CommentAuthor` from it). The new `comment-ops.ts` writes its own `buildThread`/`buildReply`/`applySetResolved`/`applyDeleteComment` instead of composing them, so the same rules now exist twice (a third near-identical copy already lives in `packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-worksheet-comments.ts`). They have already diverged: sheets' `assertNonEmpty` deliberately preserves the body verbatim ('preserve newlines / leading-trailing spaces inside non-empty content'), while the API path trims via `normalizeBody`, so the editor and the API store different text for the same input, and any future change to the root-comment/resolve rules must be made in two (or three) places. The Yorkie BigInt boundary is a legitimate backend concern, but it could wrap the shared ops rather than replace them.

verdict.reason: The finding says comment-ops.ts reimplements the sheets thread rules instead of composing them, and that the two have diverged on body trimming. Neither is in the code. comment-ops.ts:1-13 imports createThread/addReply/deleteComment/setThreadResolved from @wafflebase/sheets and every operation delegates to them: buildThread -> createThread (142-156), buildReply -> addReply (172-187), applySetResolved -> setThreadResolved (202-225), applyDeleteComment -> deleteComment and its null-means-root-comment contract (238-257). The only backend-local code is the CRDT shell the finding itself allows: in-place proxy mutation, the BigInt timestamp boundary (58-64) and proxy detachment (95-106) — i.e. it already wraps the shared ops rather than replacing them. The claimed divergence is also absent: normalizeBody (277-280) returns the body verbatim and only trims to test emptiness, identical to assertNonEmpty in packages/sheets/src/comment/thread.ts:3-9, and comment-ops.spec.ts:161-162 asserts '  hi  ' and embedded newlines are preserved. The cited exports (packages/sheets/src/index.ts:229-233, 378-381) exist but are consumed, not bypassed, so the stated cost (duplicated rules diverging, API and editor storing different text) does not arise.

finding.summary: API-created comments/replies/resolves emit no notification, and notifications.md's stated premise ('comments never pass through the backend') is now false and unrecorded
finding.evidence: `docs/design/notifications.md:16-18` states comment events are 'reported by the client and authorized by the server' *because* 'comments live inside Yorkie CRDT documents and never pass through the backend, so the client is the only party that knows a comment was posted', with callers listed at lines 210-212 as the three frontend comment controllers posting `POST /notifications/comment`. This change makes the backend itself a comment writer, but `comments.controller.ts` never calls `NotificationService.createFromComment` on create/reply/resolve. Consequence outside the codebase: a thread an agent opens with an @mention, a reply to a human's comment, and a resolve of someone's thread all notify nobody, so a mentioned collaborator is never told — the exact event class notifications v1 exists to deliver. No design doc records the new writer or the decision to skip notification.

verdict.reason: Both parts of the absence claim have direct counterexamples in the named files. (1) comments.controller.ts has a private notify() helper (lines 170-197) that calls this.notificationService.createFromComment(actorId, plan) at line 188, invoked after every comment write: PDF thread create (290-293), sheet thread create (320-323), reply (351-354), and resolve (383, guarded so reopening notifies nobody). Doc-type thread create is not an un-notified write — it is rejected with a 400 at 265-270 because the CRDT tree-position anchor cannot be minted server-side. NotificationService is imported (line 20) and injected (line 103); createFromComment exists at notification.service.ts:113. Mention planning is implemented in planCommentNotifications (532-594) with MENTION_RE at 504, so an agent-authored @mention does produce a comment_mention notification; comments.controller.spec.ts:454/487/520/538/549 asserts these calls. (2) The design doc does record the new writer: notifications.md:22-31 explicitly amends the 'comments never pass through the backend' premise ('Since v0.6.7 that premise has one exception'), and notifications.md:228-237 names ApiV1CommentsController as the fourth caller, why it calls the service directly rather than the HTTP route, and that it is not subject to UserThrottlerGuard. The stated user-facing consequence does not occur.

finding.summary: Slide ops replace the whole `root.slides` array, so the stated advantage over `PUT .../content` (surviving concurrent edits) is largely not delivered
finding.evidence: The controller's own rationale (lines 27-33 of the file, and the CLI comment at `packages/cli/src/client/http-client.ts` 'these four touch one slide each, so a concurrent edit elsewhere in the deck survives') claims these verbs avoid the lost-update problem of whole-document replace. But `apply()` reads the deck out of the CRDT, mutates a detached `MemSlidesStore` copy, and then assigns `root.slides = result.slides` — a wholesale replacement of the CRDT array object. Concurrent remote element/text edits inside other slides made in the same sync window are clobbered by that assignment, the same failure mode as `PUT content`, only narrowed from the whole root to the whole deck. A granular alternative exists in the shape the frontend Yorkie slides store uses (splice/insert on `root.slides` inside `doc.update`), and `MemSlidesStore` could still supply the constructed slide. Cost if real: silently lost collaborator work while an agent adds or moves a slide.

verdict.reason: The finding's core evidence does not exist. `apply()` (slides.controller.ts:164-196) does NOT assign `root.slides = result.slides`; it calls `applySlideChange(slides, result.change)` on the live CRDT array inside `doc.update`. The only assignment is the absent-array initializer `if (!root.slides) root.slides = []` (line 187). `applySlideChange` (slide-ops.ts:92-133) performs exactly the granular mutations the reviewer says are missing: splice(at,0,slide) for insert/insert-after, splice(at,1) for remove, and the CRDT proxy's in-place moveFront/moveAfterByIndex for move (splice pair only as a plain-array fallback). SlideChange variants carry slide ids, not indices (slide-ops.ts:47-51), resolved against the live array at apply time. MemSlidesStore is used only to construct the new slide object for insert/insert-after (slide-ops.ts:157-192) and is never written back; delete/move return id-only changes. Whole-array replacement exists only in writeSlidesRoot (slides-tree.ts:105), which this controller never imports or calls (it imports only readSlidesRoot, lines 19-22). The claimed lost-update failure mode and the claimed rationale/implementation mismatch are therefore not present.
